sourcePolicy: Fineli supplies available-carbohydrate quantities only. GI evidence is stored as individual, traceable records on the glucose scale. STRONG values must be published and ISO 26642-confirmed; they support direct food and preparation matches only. Published SUPPLEMENTARY values and explicitly sourced analogues may support a low-confidence ingredient estimate when food and preparation relevance are documented. CATEGORY_MEAN values are broad proxies, never described as measurements of the named food, and force LOW confidence. Study quality and food/preparation match quality remain separate. For a missing GI match on a positive portion below 1 g available carbohydrate per serving, omission is an editorial tolerance only when all such recipe portions sum to less than 2 g per serving; the omitted carbohydrate amount is disclosed. This is not a clinical error bound. Larger known carbohydrate portions require GI evidence. The formula is an ingredient-sum estimate, not a measurement of a prepared meal. Do not copy complete source tables or substitute unsupported foods/preparations.

sources.use: Method and eligibility standard. Clauses 4 and 5.5.1 restrict GI to tested foods and advise against GI testing below 10 g glycaemic carbohydrate per usual serving; clause 4 says heterogeneous-food GI is measured under the standard, not computed from component GIs.

source.title: International tables of glycemic index and glycemic load values 2021: a systematic review
source.table: Supplemental Table 1, entry 1861
source.qualityEvidence: Supplemental Table 1 entry 1861 identifies mashed potato, NS (China, test year 2005), GI 73 ± 3, n=10, a 50 g available-carbohydrate portion, glucose/2 h and standard timepoints. It lists venous samples but the assay method as NS. Yang et al. (2006; https://doi.org/10.3748/wjg.v12.i21.3430), the underlying primary study cited in the 2021 non-western compendium, independently reports a distinct mashed-potato row at 73.0 ± 9.2 (n=10) and a cooked-potato row at 66.4 ± 3.8. This confirms the products and values are distinct; Yang does not specify the cooking method for the cooked-potato row. Table membership supports the review's ISO-methodology classification, but the original assay details cannot be independently verified.

records.note: Closer preparation analogue for aloo-paratha's boiled-and-mashed potato filling than boiled-potato GI 66; the recipe's variety, cooling, pan-cooked dough enclosure and whole meal remain untested. This is not the GI of aloo paratha.
